newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China dissident Wang reaches San Francisco - wife.
newsitem.headline: China dissident Wang reaches San Francisco - wife.

text.p: Chinese dissident Wang Xizhe has arrived in San Francisco after flying via Russia and France in a dash for asylum in the United States, his wife said on Wednesday.
Su Jiang told Hong Kong's ATV television station that her husband arrived safely in San Francisco around 2200 GMT on October 15.
Speaking from the Chinese city of Guangzhou, Su said Wang called her half an hour after arriving in California.
"He is now in San Francisco," she said. "He is at a friend's home and should be safe."

Wang, 46, fled to Hong Kong from his home in southern China's Guangdong province last weekend, just days after authorities in Beijing arrested fellow democracy activist Liu Xiaobo and packed him off to a labour camp for three years.
He left the British colony on Monday and stopped off in France and Russia before arriving in San Francisco, Su said.
"He went round half of the globe to get there," she said.
A spokesman for the San Francisco-based Alliance for a Democratic China has said Wang will speak publicly about his escape at a news conference in San Francisco next Monday.
The dissident's wife said he had not decided what he was going to do in the United States.
Wang fled China just as communist authorities were cracking down and rounding up the last prominent members of China's shattered democracy movement.
Wang and Liu sparked reprisals against remaining dissidents last month when they demanded the impeachment of President Jiang Zemin for violating the constitution.
He is the second dissident to have fled via Hong Kong this year. Liu Gang transited Hong Kong when he fled to Boston in May after six years in prison for leading 1989 student protests.
Washington has been generous in granting asylum to Beijing's political critics since the bloody military crackdown in Tiananmen Square in 1989.
Scores, perhaps hundreds, of Chinese dissenters have fled to the West since then through Hong Kong, local activists say.
They were supported by a group called the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China.
Activists in Hong Kong fear China will shut down the escape route after the British-ruled territory reverts to Beijing in the middle of next year.
